evidence.source: Guarded Production rollout run 31534872592 applied contracts 172 to 174 from exact main 1965bf9a1e2340c6b9a96e30664ff1a61540e359, after its own API check that backup run 31532241788 and rehearsal run 31533963740 had both concluded success, and after a dry run that asserted the three migration files BY NAME with diff rather than by count. All three are ADDITIVE, so check-migration-additive.mjs ran as a GATE rather than as a report; a future reader who finds that softened back to a report should stop, because the boundary has changed. THIS IS THE FIRST PRODUCTION ROLLOUT THAT SCHEDULES A JOB, and the previous record's sentence 'It scheduled no job: 0 cron jobs before and after' was FALSE about the count when it was written: Production held SEVEN active cron jobs at contract 171, the same seven Development holds, including provider-poll-dispatch-due-targets every five minutes and provider-consume-decoded-responses at 2-59/5. The narrower claim that boundary was reaching for -- that it scheduled no NEW job -- was true. The error is recorded rather than quietly dropped because it is exactly what would lead a reader to conclude contract 174's detector is inert on Production, when it runs inside a function that is scheduled and active there. The pre-apply probe therefore refused unless Production presented exactly seven, so the post-apply ten means something. Confirmed after the apply by an independent read-only query through a different connection rather than by trusting the workflow's own output: the ledger NAMES 20260811230000_action_centre_and_reminder_drivers, 20260811233000_matchweek_settled_actions and 20260811234000_provider_calendar_change_proposals, and the total is 174. Naming the rows rather than counting them is deliberate and was learned on 11 August 2026, when a select count(*) against the Development ledger returned a stale value for roughly twenty-five minutes after a successful apply while a row-level query on the same table in the same session returned the truth immediately. cron.job now holds TEN jobs, read in full: the seven that were already there plus player-action-centre-generate at */15, player-reminder-schedule at 5-59/15 and player-reminder-reclaim-stalled at 45, all active. NOTHING SENDS, and that is verified on the INSTALLED table rather than inferred from the migration text, which are different claims: each of the three new commands carries an EMPTY argument list so process_reminder_schedule keeps its dry_run = true default, no job anywhere in the table names claim_due_reminders, and none passes false. reminder_deliveries holds no row with dry_run other than true. Contract 174's detector now runs inside the already-scheduled consume_provider_responses and will stage proposals every five minutes; provider_calendar_change_proposals holds zero rows on apply, is protected by row-level security and is granted to no browser role, detection writes NO fixture, and only admin_decide_provider_change_proposal may add or void one -- gated on require_competition_admin, refusing any fixture that already carries a result and re-checking under the row lock. The rollout asserted that the consumer calls the detector exactly once and passes NO coverage window, because a caller-declared complete span is what would let withdrawal detection propose voiding real fixtures off a partial poll. Nothing player-owned moved: 1 auth user, 3 entries and 578 season fixtures all unchanged, and every count captured before the apply was compared after it. This is SCHEMA AND SCHEDULING ONLY and claims nothing further. It did not publish Euro 2028 -- euro_publication_state() still returns hidden, publication is an owner act and EURO-001 remains a recorded defect. It launched no competition, drew no Championship and opened no Last Man Standing. It confirmed no provider result and added or voided no fixture. It imported no football, and copying Development football rows into Production remains forbidden by the contract 132 boundary. Application promotion is separately controlled and is NOT claimed by this record: the deployed site remains at contract 145, so no browser can reach any of this yet.
